claim: Triplet-scalar H++ can evade prompt same-sign dilepton / W+W+ searches in three regimes: (i) long-lived H++ (c tau ~ 0.1-100 mm) - in type-II seesaw only for m ~ 100-150 GeV near the ll/WW crossover, but up to ~TeV if the triplet is fermiophobic (y_ll = 0, v_t <~ 1e-4 GeV) (arXiv:2608.27251 abstract, Sec. 2, Fig. 1; arXiv:1808.00943 Sec. 2.1, Fig. 1; arXiv:2410.19561 for GM H5++); (ii) compressed positive hierarchy (1 <~ dM <~ 30 GeV, v_t ~ 1e-7-1e-3 GeV) where cascades H++ -> H+ W* -> H0/A0 W* W* dominate and H0/A0 -> nu nu, giving soft same-sign leptons + MET (+ISR) (arXiv:2305.06889, arXiv:2603.15882); (iii) tau-rich ll final states fixed by neutrino data.
framework: Type-II seesaw: Y=1 SU(2)_L triplet Delta with Yukawa (f_L)_ab L^T C i sigma2 Delta L, m_nu = sqrt2 f_L v_L (1808.00943 Eq. 2.7-2.8); trilinear mu H^T Delta H induces v_t; masses split by one quartic (lambda_4/lambda_5 depending on convention) giving equal-spacing M_H++^2 - M_H+^2 = M_H+^2 - M_H0^2 (1808.00943 Eq. 2.5-2.6; 2603.15882 Sec. 2). Georgi-Machacek variant: custodial fiveplet H5 (fermiophobic at tree level, couplings to VV ~ s_H). Left-right models: H_R++ with heavy-neutrino Yukawas.
assumptions: Drell-Yan (plus photon-initiated, W*-mediated H++H-) production fixed by gauge quantum numbers; no model freedom in sigma(m) up to PDF/QCD uncertainties.

(i) type-II: Yukawas fixed by oscillation data -> f_L v_L = 0.027 eV (NH, m1=0) or 0.048 eV (IH, m3=0) (1808.00943 Eq. 2.14); cascades negligible, i.e. |M_H++ - M_H+| <~ 1 GeV or H++ lightest (1808.00943 Sec. 2.1).
(i) fermiophobic: y_ll = 0 so the triplet plays no role in neutrino masses; H++ -> W(*)W(*) only, Gamma ~ G_F^2 v_t^2 M^3 (1808.00943 Eq. 2.11); other triplet states heavier or degenerate.
(ii) compressed: H++ heaviest (Delta M > 0), v_t <= ~1e-4 GeV so H0/A0 -> nu nu (2305.06889 Sec. I; 2603.15882 Sec. 3).
(iii) BR pattern requires the same triplet to generate all neutrino masses (pure type-II).
controlling_parameters: Delta M = M_H++ - M_H+ (sign and size)
Yukawa matrix f_L (= m_nu/(sqrt2 v_t); depends on hierarchy, lightest mass m0, Majorana phases)
in GM: s_H, m5 and H5^0 -> gamma gamma loop parameters
Width ratios ll : WW : H+W* ~ (m_nu/v_t)^2 : (v_t/v_d)^2 (M/v_d)^2 : max(dM,0)^5/(v_d^2 M^3) (2603.15882 Eq. 16)
robust_predictions: Same-sign charge-2 parent: Drell-Yan pair production with known cross section; a doubly charged displaced vertex has net charge +-2 and the incoming track (if long enough) has ~4x MIP dE/dx.

In type-II with neutrino-mass Yukawas, Gamma_ll x Gamma_WW is fixed by m_nu, so the lifetime has a maximum at v_t ~ O(0.1-1 MeV); long-lived (mm-m) H++ only for M <~ 150-160 GeV (below on-shell WW) (1808.00943 Fig. 1; 2608.27251 Fig. 1a).

Fermiophobic case: c tau grows monotonically as v_t -> 0; long-lived for v_t <~ 1e-4 GeV above WW threshold, up to TeV masses (2608.27251 Sec. 2, Fig. 1b). Small v_t is technically natural (mu -> 0 restores a U(1) acting on Delta) and with y_ll = 0 and no other L-violation, lepton number with L_Delta = 0 is exact, so y_ll is not regenerated (reviewer argument; 2608.27251 asserts higher-order effects induce y_ll - this depends on the UV, UNVERIFIED).

Compressed regime: cascade dominance for dM >~ 10 GeV and 1e-5 <~ v_t <~ 1e-2 GeV (2603.15882 Sec. 3, Fig. 1); EWPD (T parameter) caps |dM| <~ 40 GeV (2603.15882 Sec. 3), so W in cascades is always off-shell -> soft leptons.

Flavour pattern: BR(H++ -> l_a l_b) proportional to |(m_nu)_ab|^2/(1+delta_ab); for NH with m1 ~ 0, (m_nu)_ee is small so mu mu, tau tau, mu tau dominate -> tau-containing channels carry a large fraction (qualitative; numbers UNVERIFIED).
model_dependent_predictions: Fermiophobic H++ at TeV masses (no neutrino-mass link; motivation reduced to GM/composite/custodial models).

Presence and size of cascades (depends on a free quartic); GM fiveplet degenerate at tree level, radiative/custodial-breaking splittings could open H5++ -> H5+ pi+ (soft) modes competing with v_t-suppressed WW decays (reviewer concern, UNVERIFIED).

In GM, H5^0 -> gamma gamma is not s_H-suppressed and excludes 70 <~ m5 <~ 108 GeV in the low-m5 benchmark independent of H5++ lifetime (2410.19561 Sec. II), but can be cancelled between W and H3 loops.
Exact tau fraction (hierarchy, m0, Majorana phases); LR-model H_R++ flavour pattern unrelated to light-neutrino data.
H0/A0 -> nu nu (invisible) only for v_t <~ 1e-4 GeV; otherwise bb, ZZ, hh, etc.

theory_uncertainties: Production cross section: QCD K-factors and the photon-initiated component (charge^4 enhanced for H++) depend on photon PDF; size UNVERIFIED (~10-20%?).
Off-shell four-body W*W* and cascade widths near thresholds (1808.00943 App. A) - affects c tau mapping at M < 160 GeV.
Radiative mass splittings among nearly degenerate triplet/fiveplet components (O(100 MeV-1 GeV), UNVERIFIED) can open soft-pion transitions that change the long-lived signature.
Flavour BRs for (iii) uncertain through m0, hierarchy and Majorana phases.
Hadronic W* fragmentation in a displaced charged vertex - vertex charge and track multiplicity modelling for a charged parent is not standard in existing DV tools (2608.27251 Sec. 3.2.2).
distinctiveness: (i) A charged-2 track terminating in a displaced vertex of same-sign leptons/W* products (net vertex charge +-2), pair-produced: distinct from neutral-LLP DV, from singly-charged disappearing tracks (winos) and from opposite-charge displaced dileptons. (ii) Same-sign soft dileptons with low m_ll + MET + ISR from a single parent's two same-sign W*, versus compressed higgsinos which give opposite-sign soft dileptons. (iii) Lepton-flavour pattern in H++ decays tied to neutrino oscillation parameters - a unique consistency test of type-II seesaw.
caveats: Target (i) in its broad mass range (up to ~TeV) relies on the fermiophobic assumption; for the neutrino-mass-motivated type-II only 100-150 GeV is long-lived, a narrow window.
Target (ii) is well motivated within type-II and consistent with EWPD; sensitivity is driven by soft-lepton reconstruction rather than theory.
Target (iii) is theoretically robust in pure type-II; LR or GM variants change or remove the pattern.
2608.27251 (Aug 2026) and 2603.15882 (2026) are recent phenomenology papers; experimental coverage not assessed here (theory gate only).
